answer.text: Primarily bonds and other interest-rate-sensitive assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Source pp.66-67 define interest rate risk as the risk arising from changes in market interest rates and explain the inverse relationship between bond prices and yields. Source p.147 notes that interest rates are a common risk factor affecting investments directly or indirectly, so bonds are the primary, but not the only, affected asset class. The Trap: Saying the risk affects only equity, only commodities, or only currency misses the bond-specific sensitivity that pp.66-67 emphasise. Note: Duration captures the sensitivity of bond prices to changes in interest rates per pp.66-67.
